articles.title: Habitação consome a maior parte do orçamento das famílias do RN | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa de Orçamentos Familiares 2024-2025 mostra que mais da metade da população do estado vive nas duas faixas de menor rendimento. Gastos com moradia e comida lideram despesas.
articles.summary: Pesquisa do IBGE detalha o orçamento das famílias do Rio Grande do Norte. Habitação e alimentação lideram despesas, evidenciando alta desigualdade de renda no estado.
articles.body:
Natal vista aérea da cidade — Foto: Secom/Natal

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) divulgou no dia 27 os primeiros resultados da Pesquisa de Orçamentos Familiares (POF) 2024-2025. O levantamento retrata como as famílias brasileiras vivem, consomem e organizam seus gastos. No Rio Grande do Norte, os dados apontam que a habitação é a principal despesa da população, seguida pela alimentação, evidenciando também um cenário de alta desigualdade de renda no estado.

Em média, 22,7% das despesas das famílias potiguares eram voltadas para a habitação, o que inclui aluguel, condomínio, manutenção do lar e taxas de serviços básicos como energia, água e internet. O percentual representa um valor médio mensal de R$ 1.547,53.

O custo com moradia varia conforme a renda, mas permanece como o maior peso no orçamento na maioria dos casos. Famílias que ganham até dois salários-mínimos (R$ 3.036) gastavam em média 33,8% das despesas com habitação (R$ 730,30). Entre as que recebem de dois a seis salários, o índice variou de 24,1% a 26,9%.

A situação muda nas famílias com renda entre seis e dez salários-mínimos (de R$ 9.108 a R$ 15.180). Nesse grupo, o transporte assumiu o topo das despesas (23,3%), seguido pela habitação (17,6%). Já entre as famílias com renda superior a 25 salários-mínimos (mais de R$ 37.950), os gastos com transporte (16,2%) e habitação (16,1%) apresentaram proporções semelhantes.

A alimentação comprometeu, em média, 13,1% do orçamento das famílias do estado. No entanto, o impacto é maior entre os mais pobres. Nas casas com rendimento de até dois salários-mínimos, a comida representava 19,1% das despesas (R$ 412,87). Entre os mais ricos, a participação caiu para 8,5%, embora o valor absoluto gasto por esse grupo seja de quatro a quase oito vezes maior do que o despendido pelas famílias de menor renda.

A compra de carnes, vísceras e pescados correspondeu a 12,3% das despesas com alimentação no domicílio, com média mensal de R$ 109,94. O valor foi de R$ 55,45 entre os mais pobres e chegou a R$ 281,25 entre os mais ricos. A pesquisa registrou disparidades semelhantes no consumo de frutas, legumes, verduras e tubérculos, com as classes mais altas gastando até cinco vezes mais que as mais baixas. O gasto com cereais e leguminosas foi o mais equilibrado entre os diferentes estratos, variando de R$ 25,07 a R$ 46,46.

O hábito de comer fora de casa também reflete a diferença de renda. Famílias que ganham mais de R$ 37.950 destinavam 57% das despesas de alimentação para refeições fora do domicílio, um custo médio de R$ 1.841,45 por mês. Em contrapartida, as famílias que recebem até R$ 3.036 gastavam R$ 87,09 (21,1%) com alimentação fora de casa. A maioria da população do estado destina entre 60% e 80% do orçamento alimentar para o consumo no próprio domicílio.

O rendimento total e a variação patrimonial das famílias potiguares alcançaram uma média de R$ 7.796,93, apontada no levantamento como a maior do Nordeste. Contudo, a concentração de renda é expressiva. Enquanto o grupo de até dois salários-mínimos teve média de R$ 1.964,31, a fatia com mais de 25 salários-mínimos registrou R$ 66.876,30, um valor 34 vezes maior.

Mais da metade da população do estado (52,65%) vivia nas duas faixas de menor rendimento, somando 668.416 famílias. No extremo oposto, apenas 2,11% das famílias (26.825) integravam a classe de renda mais alta.

A analista da POF, Isabel dos Santos, afirma que o contraste evidencia a concentração dos rendimentos. "As disparidades de rendimento entre as classes podem estar revelando peso diferente de fontes de rendimento. E, se a distância entre as classes é alta, podemos também dizer que há uma tendência à desigualdade", disse.

articles.title: Justiça condena faculdades por oferta irregular de cursos no MA | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão anula diplomas, determina a devolução dos valores pagos pelos estudantes e proíbe instituições de oferecer cursos de graduação e pós-graduação sem autorização no Maranhão.
articles.summary: Decisão anula diplomas, determina a devolução dos valores pagos pelos estudantes e proíbe instituições de oferecer cursos de graduação e pós-graduação sem autorização no Maranhão.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A Justiça Federal condenou duas instituições de ensino por oferta irregular de cursos de graduação em Penalva e municípios vizinhos, no Maranhão. A decisão anulou diplomas e certificados vinculados aos cursos irregulares, determinou a devolução dos valores pagos pelos estudantes e proibiu as faculdades de oferecer cursos de graduação e pós-graduação no estado sem autorização do Ministério da Educação (MEC).

A condenação é resultado de uma ação civil pública do Ministério Público Federal (MPF) contra a Faculdade Associada de Ciências, Tecnologia e Letras (Facitel) e a Faculdade Cidade de Guanhães (Facig), com sede em Minas Gerais.

As investigações começaram após a Prefeitura de Penalva identificar a necessidade de verificar a autenticidade de diplomas apresentados por servidores municipais para obter progressão na carreira.

Segundo o MPF, a Facitel oferecia cursos livres e de extensão, como Pedagogia e Letras, mas atraía estudantes com promessas de obtenção de diplomas de graduação.

Consultas ao Ministério da Educação (MEC) confirmaram que a Facitel não tinha autorização para oferecer cursos superiores nem emitir diplomas. Já a Facig, com sede em Guanhães, em Minas Gerais, tinha autorização apenas para oferecer cursos presenciais em seu campus.

Apesar das restrições, a instituição mineira validava os cursos oferecidos pela Facitel no Maranhão, permitindo a emissão irregular de diplomas.

De acordo com a sentença, após a descoberta das irregularidades, o responsável pela Facitel chegou a reunir estudantes em uma sede sindical para tentar recolher diplomas falsos entregues a uma turma de Letras e substituí-los por certificados.

As duas instituições não apresentaram defesa durante o processo.

Estudantes deverão receber dinheiro de volta

A Justiça determinou que as instituições devolvam integralmente os valores pagos pelos estudantes prejudicados, incluindo taxas de inscrição, matrícula e mensalidades. Os valores serão calculados individualmente e atualizados pela taxa Selic.

As faculdades também foram condenadas ao pagamento de R$ 100 mil por danos morais coletivos. O valor será destinado ao Fundo de Defesa dos Direitos Difusos (FDD).

Além disso, as instituições estão proibidas de oferecer cursos de graduação e pós-graduação no Maranhão sem autorização do MEC, realizar matrículas, promover vestibulares ou cobrar mensalidades relacionadas a essas formações.

Em caso de descumprimento das determinações, será aplicada multa de R$ 50 mil por infração.

A sentença também determina que a Facitel e a Facig divulguem a condenação em seus sites e redes sociais durante 90 dias consecutivos. As instituições ainda deverão publicar a decisão em dois jornais de ampla circulação no Maranhão, após o encerramento definitivo do processo.

A sentença será submetida à revisão obrigatória por uma instância superior. As instituições também podem recorrer da decisão.

articles.title: Fumaça de queimadas no Pará avança e encobre cidades do Amazonas | G1
articles.standfirst: Cidade registrou índice de poluição quase 20 vezes acima do limite recomendado pela OMS. Poluição viaja centenas de quilômetros e afeta a visibilidade de municípios do estado vizinho.
articles.summary: Com a qualidade do ar em Santarém 20 vezes pior que o limite da OMS, o município registra 110 casos de intoxicação e a suspensão de aulas presenciais na Ufopa.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A fumaça de queimadas em Santarém e municípios do Pará avança e encobre também cidades do Amazonas desde o início desta semana. Nesta sexta-feira (27), o município paraense registrou o pior Índice de Qualidade do Ar (AQI), com em 181 pontos - a situação na cidade é classificada como insalubre. Os ventos seriam responsáveis por transportar as partículas ao Estado vizinho.

♨️ AQI (Índice de Qualidade do Ar) usado pelo IQAir vai de 0 a 500. Quanto maior o número, pior a qualidade do ar e maior o risco à saúde. Acima de 150 na escala o ar é considerado insalubre.

O Programa de Queimadas do Instituto Nacional de Pesquisas Espaciais (INPE) mostra que mais da metade dos focos de incêndio do Brasil foram registrados no Pará na últimas 48 horas. Foram 1.513 focos. No Amazonas, por exemplo, foram 78 no mesmo período.

A falta de chuva no Pará há mais de 90 dias agrava o cenário, deixando a mata seca e propícia para o fogo se espalhar.

“Nós estamos há mais de três meses sem ocorrência de chuva abrangente no município de Santarém, e a vegetação está altamente vulnerável às queimadas devido ao acúmulo de material combustível disponível”, ressalta Alex Santos.

Cidade registrou índice de poluição quase 20 vezes acima do limite recomendado pela OMS. — Foto: Waldiney Ferreira/TV Tapajós

O monitoramento do site IQAir apontou que Santarém registrou uma concentração de partículas finas (PM2.5) de 98,5 microgramas por metro cúbico, número quase 20 vezes maior do que o limite anual recomendado pela Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS). Essas partículas microscópicas conseguem penetrar profundamente no sistema respiratório e chegar à corrente sanguínea.

Juruti e Terra Santa também estão em situação preocupante, com o ar classificado como "não saudável para grupos sensíveis", como crianças, idosos e gestantes.

Veja o ranking da qualidade do ar no Oeste do Pará (dados das 9h de sexta-feira):

2º Juruti: AQI 116 (Não saudável para grupos sensíveis)

3º Terra Santa: AQI 115 (Não saudável para grupos sensíveis)

Os números revelam que a poluição não está concentrada apenas em Santarém. Embora os demais municípios apresentem índices inferiores, a presença de partículas finas na atmosfera representa um risco que exige atenção, principalmente para quem permanece exposto à fumaça durante longos períodos.

Em Santarém, a situação é particularmente grave. A concentração de PM2.5 registrada nesta sexta-feira chegou a 98,5 µg/m³. Essas partículas microscópicas conseguem penetrar profundamente no sistema respiratório e alcançar a corrente sanguínea, aumentando os riscos de agravamento de doenças pulmonares e cardiovasculares.

A plataforma IQAir mede a qualidade do ar em uma escala que vai de 0 a 500 pontos, onde números maiores representam riscos mais graves à saúde. Índices acima de 150 entram na faixa considerada insalubre, quando a poluição começa a afetar toda a população, e não apenas os grupos de risco.

É neste cenário de alerta que se encontra Santarém, com 181 pontos. Já os municípios de Juruti, com 116, e Terra Santa, com 115 pontos, estão na categoria "não saudável para grupos sensíveis", que engloba crianças, idosos, gestantes e pessoas com problemas respiratórios ou cardíacos.

Índice da qualidade do ar em Santarem — Foto: Reprodução

As temperaturas máximas previstas também são elevadas, chegando a 37°C no sábado (28) e no domingo (29). A combinação de calor intenso, baixa umidade e poluição atmosférica aumenta o desconforto e os riscos à saúde, especialmente durante atividades físicas ao ar livre.

A fumaça registrada em Santarém nos últimos dias é resultado de queimadas locais somadas aos incêndios em municípios vizinhos no oeste do Pará. Consequentemente, a fumaça acaba sendo levada também para o Amazonas. Condições meteorológicas favorecem o transporte dessa poluição por centenas de quilômetros.

De acordo com o meteorologista Alex Santos, professor da Universidade Federal do Oeste do Pará (Ufopa), a direção dos ventos explica o fenômeno. Cidades como Almeirim, Prainha, Monte Alegre e Alenquer, situadas a leste, influenciam diretamente no clima de Santarém.

“O vento aqui em Santarém é predominantemente de leste, mudando em alguns horários para nordeste. Todos os municípios que se posicionam a leste do município de Santarém têm uma influência direta no transporte de materiais particulados”, explica o meteorologista.

Isso significa, na prática, que o vento vem do leste e sopra em direção ao oeste. Assim, partículas presentes em Santarém, ou trazidas de municípios a leste de Santarém, podem continuar sendo transportadas para oeste, em direção ao Amazonas.

A falta de chuva há mais de 90 dias agrava o cenário, deixando a mata seca e propícia para o fogo se espalhar.

Para tentar conter a crise, a Prefeitura de Santarém publicou o Decreto nº 792/2026, que proíbe temporariamente o uso do fogo. O município também comprou equipamentos como sopradores e bombas costais para brigadistas, além de disponibilizar veículos para fiscalização.

Aeronave KC-390 Millennium, da Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) ajuda no combate às queimadas em Santarém — Foto: Divulgação/FAB

Com a chegada de aeronaves da Força Aérea Brasileira (FAB) para combater os incêndios na região, a prefeitura passou a fornecer o suporte logístico, enviando um caminhão-pipa de 20 mil litros para abastecer os reservatórios de água dos aviões.

A secretária municipal de Meio Ambiente, Vânia Portela, reforça que o problema exige uma união de esforços na região.

“A fumaça que estamos enfrentando em Santarém evidencia que os impactos das queimadas ultrapassam os limites territoriais dos municípios. Seguimos atuando no enfrentamento aos focos locais, mobilizando equipes, disponibilizando recursos e apoiando as instituições que trabalham diretamente no combate ao fogo”, destaca a secretária.

A gravidade da situação também aparece nos dados do monitoramento realizado pela Universidade Federal do Oeste do Pará (Ufopa). Mesmo com a melhora registrada entre quarta e quinta-feira, a instituição decidiu manter, nesta sexta-feira, o Protocolo Institucional de Emergência em sete dos oito municípios onde possui campi.

Os indicadores do Laboratório de Agrometeorologia com Modelagem da Bioeconomia e Diagnóstico Ambiental (Lambda) mostram uma situação ainda mais preocupante em alguns municípios. Itaituba registra IQAr de 317 pontos, classificação péssima, enquanto Oriximiná aparece com 264 e Rurópolis com 233, ambos também na categoria péssima.

Nos demais municípios com protocolo acionado, os índices são de 196 em Juruti, 196 em Monte Alegre, 192 em Óbidos e 148 em Santarém. Alenquer apresenta 177 pontos, classificação muito ruim, e permanece sob monitoramento, sem acionamento do protocolo de emergência.

É importante destacar que esses números pertencem ao sistema de monitoramento da Ufopa e não devem ser confundidos com os índices AQI do IQAir apresentados no ranking regional, pois são metodologias e escalas distintas.

A Portaria nº 629/2026 estabelece medidas emergenciais, incluindo a suspensão das atividades acadêmicas presenciais dos cursos de graduação e pós-graduação nos campi atingidos, além de alterações no funcionamento de serviços e redução dos horários do transporte intercampus.

O retorno às atividades presenciais está previsto para segunda-feira (30), mas condicionado à manutenção de níveis seguros de qualidade do ar. A Reitoria continuará publicando avaliações diárias para decidir sobre a continuidade ou revisão das medidas.

O avanço da fumaça está diretamente relacionado à persistência dos incêndios florestais e das queimadas na região. Dados referentes ao período de 25 a 26 de novembro apontam que o Pará registrou 1.513 ocorrências de focos de incêndio.

Sala de Monitoramento integra esforços de prevenção e combate aos incêndios florestais. — Foto: Divulgação: PMS

Em Santarém, os registros de monitoramento apresentam ocorrências de longa duração e grandes áreas atingidas. Um dos registros aponta incêndio iniciado em 1º de outubro, com duração de 56 dias e área estimada em 1.693,34 hectares, tendo como último foco identificado o dia 25 de novembro.

Outro registro indica incêndio iniciado em 4 de outubro, com duração de 53 dias e área de 23.062,91 hectares, com identificação de atividade de fogo até 26 de novembro.

Os dados reforçam a dimensão do problema ambiental enfrentado pelo município, que continua convivendo com episódios de fumaça e deterioração da qualidade do ar.

A crise ambiental deixou de ser apenas uma preocupação relacionada à preservação da floresta e passou a produzir consequências concretas na saúde pública.

Dados do Núcleo de Vigilância em Saúde da Secretaria Municipal de Saúde de Santarém apontam 179 notificações de moradores com problemas relacionados à intoxicação por fumaça no segundo semestre de 2026.

A evolução dos registros demonstra o agravamento da situação. Em agosto, foi registrada uma ocorrência. Em setembro, nenhuma notificação foi contabilizada. Em outubro, foram 22 casos. Já em novembro, o número saltou para 87, concentrando quase 80% de todas as notificações do período.

O aumento coincide com a intensificação das queimadas e dos episódios de poluição atmosférica. A fumaça tem provocado procura por atendimento médico, ampliando a pressão sobre as unidades de saúde e a Unidade de Pronto Atendimento (UPA).

O neurocirurgião Erik Jennings Simões também fez um alerta público sobre os efeitos da exposição prolongada à poluição. O médico chama atenção para os riscos cardiovasculares e neurológicos associados à inalação de partículas finas e defende que o problema seja tratado como uma emergência de saúde pública.

Em Óbidos, a administração municipal já adotou medidas preventivas diante da fumaça. A Secretaria Municipal da Mulher suspendeu temporariamente atividades físicas realizadas em espaços externos, incluindo aulões de dança e aulas de pilates solo.

Atividades físicas foram suspensas em Óbidos — Foto: Divulgação

A decisão considera os altos índices de poluição atmosférica e as disposições do Decreto Municipal nº 384/2026-GAB, que declarou situação de emergência no município.

Os atendimentos administrativos e presenciais na sede da secretaria continuam normalmente. As atividades externas somente serão retomadas quando os órgãos competentes considerarem que a qualidade do ar voltou a níveis seguros.

Para ampliar o acesso da população às informações sobre a qualidade do ar, a Ufopa disponibiliza gratuitamente a plataforma FioAres Ar, que permite acompanhar indicadores ambientais em tempo real em cinco cidades amazônicas: Santarém, Belém, Manaus, Porto Velho e Rio Branco.

Plataforma ajuda a acompanhar a situação da fumaça em Santarém. — Foto: Divulgação

A ferramenta apresenta o Índice de Qualidade do Ar, a concentração de material particulado fino PM2.5, a temperatura, a umidade relativa e o histórico das últimas 24 horas.

Segundo a professora Ana Carla Gomes, a iniciativa busca democratizar o acesso à informação e ajudar as pessoas a reduzir a exposição à poluição. A recomendação é consultar os indicadores antes de realizar caminhadas, corridas ou outras atividades ao ar livre.

Enquanto a fumaça continua avançando sobre os municípios do Baixo Amazonas, os dados revelam uma realidade que exige respostas urgentes do poder público. A deterioração da qualidade do ar, o aumento das notificações de intoxicação e as medidas emergenciais adotadas por instituições de ensino mostram que a crise já ultrapassou os limites de um problema ambiental.

articles.title: Descomplicando Carreiras: conheça os caminhos do Jornalismo | G1

articles.summary: Ceiça Ricarte fala sobre a atuação do jornalista, os desafios da profissão e as possibilidades de carreira na comunicação.
articles.body:
Descomplicando carreiras — Foto: Reprodução

O Jornalismo está presente em diferentes momentos do nosso dia a dia, levando informação e ajudando a sociedade a compreender os acontecimentos. Com possibilidades de atuação na televisão, no rádio, na internet, em jornais e em empresas, a profissão acompanha as transformações nos meios de comunicação e nas formas de consumir conteúdo.

No episódio desta semana do Descomplicando Carreiras, Pedro Gomes conversa com Ceiça Ricarte sobre a profissão de jornalista, os desafios da área e as oportunidades no mercado de trabalho. A convidada apresenta diferentes possibilidades de atuação e compartilha conhecimentos sobre uma carreira que tem na informação e na comunicação seus principais pilares.

A série Descomplicando Carreiras faz parte do projeto Aprova com o Sagrado e apresenta aos estudantes profissionais de diferentes áreas, ajudando quem ainda está em dúvida a conhecer melhor as opções antes de escolher uma carreira.

O Ministério das Relações Exteriores (MRE) informou que não havia sido notificado sobre a morte do lutador Gustavo Ferro na Ucrânia até a tarde desta sexta-feira (27).

Em nota enviada ao g1 , o governo brasileiro afirmou que a Embaixada do Brasil em Kiev permanece à disposição para prestar assistência consular, caso seja solicitada.

Segundo o Itamaraty, o atendimento consular prestado pelo Estado brasileiro ocorre a partir do contato do cidadão interessado ou, dependendo do caso, de familiares. O ministério ressaltou que a atuação consular segue a legislação internacional e nacional.

O ministério acrescentou que a prestação de assistência consular em situações que envolvem brasileiros engajados em forças armadas de outros países possui particularidades relacionadas às obrigações assumidas no momento do alistamento e às condições existentes nas áreas de conflito.

O Itamaraty destacou ainda que vem alertando brasileiros sobre os riscos decorrentes da situação de segurança na Ucrânia desde maio de 2025, quando publicou um alerta consular desencorajando visitas às regiões próximas às frentes de combate.

Em julho do mesmo ano, foi emitido um novo alerta consular, atualizado em setembro de 2026, recomendando que brasileiros recusassem ofertas de trabalho e convites para participação em exércitos estrangeiros.

Em nota, o governo brasileiro afirmou que a Embaixada do Brasil em Kiev permanece à disposição para prestar assistência consular, caso seja solicitada. — Foto: Valter Campanato/ Agência Brasil

Gustavo Ferro , tricampeão brasileiro de muay thai, morreu aos 31 anos enquanto participava de operações militares na guerra na Ucrânia. A informação foi confirmada pela família.

Nascido no Rio de Janeiro, o atleta residia há 20 anos em Cabo Frio com os pais e com a irmã. Era conhecido no cenário das artes marciais e acumulava títulos nacionais na modalidade.

A morte ocorreu durante um combate no conflito entre Ucrânia e Rússia. A família recebeu a notícia por meio de pessoas que estavam com o brasileiro no país europeu.

articles.summary: Justiça também determinou a retirada do vídeo das redes sociais e uma retratação pública.
articles.body:
O vice-prefeito de Ubá , Rômulo Silva Rodrigues (Republicanos), foi condenado a pagar R$ 10 mil de indenização por danos morais ao prefeito José Damato (PSD) após postar um vídeo nas redes sociais acusando-o de participar de uma reunião que planejaria o atentado contra um ex-assessor da Prefeitura, que foi baleado mas sobreviveu.

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

A Justiça também determinou a retirada do vídeo, proibiu a republicação da acusação e ordenou que o vice-prefeito fizesse uma retratação pública. O caso foi julgado na Unidade Jurisdicional Única do Juizado Especial da Comarca de Ubá e não cabe mais recurso.

No vídeo, Rômulo dizia ter recebido informações sobre o planejamento do crime, com participação do prefeito e outros representantes da prefeitura.

Vice-prefeito de Ubá, Rômulo Silva Rodrigues, foi condenado a indenizar o prefeito José Damato por danos morais após acusação feita nas redes sociais — Foto: Reproduções Rede Sociais

Ao entrar com a ação, o prefeito alegou que a acusação era falsa e ultrapassava os limites da liberdade de expressão e da crítica política, prejudicando sua honra e imagem. O vice-prefeito não compareceu à audiência nem apresentou defesa.

Na sentença, publicada em outubro, a magistrada reconheceu que agentes políticos estão sujeitos a críticas mais intensas, mas considerou que a divulgação de acusações de natureza criminosa sem provas ultrapassa os limites da liberdade de expressão. Por isso, condenou ao vice-prefeito pelo pagamento da indenização e pela postagem de retratação pública.

Em nota, a defesa de Rômulo afirmou que o vice-prefeito foi condenado à revelia, ou seja, sem apresentar defesa no processo. Segundo os advogados, a assessoria jurídica anterior deixou de atuar no caso por questões de oposição política. A atual defesa informou ainda que orientou Rômulo a cumprir as decisões judiciais e a evitar novos processos.

O g1 não conseguiu contato com os advogados do prefeito até a publicação desta reportagem.

articles.title: Espanha encerra campanha eleitoral; Sánchez tenta frear a direita e a extrema direita | G1

articles.summary: Partido do premiê espanhol aparece atrás da oposição nas pesquisas de intenção de voto. Pleito está marcado para domingo (29).
articles.body:

A Espanha encerra nesta sexta-feira (27) a campanha antes das eleições de domingo (29), nas quais o primeiro-ministro socialista Pedro Sánchez espera desafiar as pesquisas favoráveis à direita, que pode chegar ao poder com o apoio da extrema direita.

Se a extrema direita chegar ao governo após as eleições legislativas antecipadas, inicialmente previstas para meados de 2027, será a primeira vez que isso acontece na Espanha desde a morte do ditador Francisco Franco, em 1975.

A votação na quarta maior economia da zona do euro será acompanhada de perto devido à proximidade de outras eleições em países importantes da Europa, como França, Itália e Polônia.

Uma mudança de signo político na Espanha reforçaria o avanço das forças conservadoras e de extrema direita na região, onde Sánchez é uma das vozes mais visíveis da esquerda.

Primeiro-ministro da Espanha, Pedro Sánchez (à esquerda), e líder da oposição e do Partido Popular (PP), Alberto Núñez Feijó, durante debate televisivo na Espanha em 26 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Juan Medina

No último debate exibido na televisão na noite de quinta-feira (26), Sánchez (PSOE) apresentou o pleito de domingo como uma decisão entre "dois caminhos muito diferentes": o da " Espanha próspera", que ele encarnaria com seus avanços sociais, e o de uma " Espanha de retrocesso, cortes e congelamento de salários", caso a direita e a extrema direita governem o país.

Alberto Núñez Feijóo, líder do Partido Popular (PP, direita) e favorito nas pesquisas, concentrou os ataques à gestão econômica e aos escândalos de corrupção que atingiram o Executivo. "Sánchez não responde a nada. Só foge", disse.

Por sua vez, o candidato do partido de extrema direita Vox, Santiago Abascal, responsabilizou o governo por ter promovido uma imigração em larga escala que, segundo ele, agravou a crise de habitação - uma das principais preocupações dos eleitores -, deteriorou os serviços públicos e aumentou a insegurança.

A imigração virou um tema crucial da campanha , em um país onde milhares de estrangeiros, principalmente latino-americanos, aguardam uma resposta a seus pedidos de regularização no âmbito de um processo extraordinário impulsionado pelo governo socialista.

Últimos comícios em Madri, Sevilha e Valência

Na noite de sexta-feira, Sánchez encerrará a campanha em Madri, enquanto Feijóo fará um comício em Sevilha, na Andaluzia. Abascal discursará em Valência, leste do país.

Para a cientista política Paloma Román, da Universidade Complutense de Madri, as últimas horas de campanha serão decisivas para o socialista, que busca "mobilizar os abstencionistas", geralmente de esquerda, diante de uma direita que concentrou sua mensagem no lema "tirar Sánchez" do poder.

Segundo as pesquisas, o PP será o mais votado, mas a distância para o PSOE caiu nas últimas semanas. O partido conservador não alcançaria maioria absoluta no Congresso, o que poderia levá-lo a buscar o apoio da extrema direita, terceira força política do país e que poderia quase dobrar o número de cadeiras no Parlamento.

PP e Vox governam juntos várias regiões.

Crise migratória em Ceuta em julho deste ano. — Foto: AP/Antonio Sempere

Após mais de oito anos à frente do governo, Sánchez enfrenta sua eleição mais difícil, consolidado como figura internacional da esquerda após seus embates com Donald Trump e Benjamin Netanyahu. Mas, dentro da Espanha , ele está muito desgastado por uma série de escândalos de corrupção que envolvem antigos colaboradores próximos e membros de sua família.

O socialista de 54 anos, que se orgulha do dinamismo da economia espanhola apesar das persistentes desigualdades, tenta tirar proveito do descontentamento provocado pela crise de acesso à moradia. De fato, ele antecipou as eleições quando o Congresso derrubou um pacote de medidas para enfrentar a situação.

A oposição critica Sánchez por não conseguir frear a escalada dos preços da habitação , nem do custo de vida em geral. Também reprova a gestão socialista por não ter antecipado a crise migratória em Ceuta no mês de julho, quando dezenas de milhares de migrantes entraram no território espanhol no norte da África a partir de Marrocos.

Além disso, acusa o governo socialista de falta de investimentos ao recordar os dois acidentes de trens de alta velocidade que deixaram 115 mortos neste ano, um deles em e outro em outubro.

Feijóo, de 65 anos, destaca seu balanço à frente da região noroeste da Galícia durante 13 anos e afirma que pretende virar a página da era Pedro Sánchez com "verdade, decência e gestão".

Equipes resgatam vítimas de colisão entre trens de alta velocidade em Urda, na Espanha, no dia 28 de outubro de 2026 — Foto: Javier Soriano/AFP

articles.summary: HYDERABAD: A family from Hyderabad has been awarded Rs 70,000 by a Telangana consumer commission after an airline cancelled their direct flights to
articles.body: HYDERABAD: A family from Hyderabad has been awarded Rs 70,000 by a Telangana consumer commission after an airline cancelled their direct flights to Thailand and shifted them to connecting flights, leaving them with stopovers of up to 11 hours. The commission held the airline responsible for deficiency in service, observing that it had failed to establish any valid reason for scrapping the original flight schedule. While the family eventually made the trip on the revised flights, the commission found that the passengers had been left to bear the inconvenience and expenses arising from the changes.The complainant had spent Rs 1,16,477 on round-trip tickets for four passengers travelling between Hyderabad and Phuket from June 6 to 13, 2026. Another Rs 2,949 was paid for additional baggage allowance. Having booked non-stop flights, the family had also made advance reservations at a hotel in Phuket, which were non-refundable. The travel plans changed on May 21, when the airline informed the passengers that their booked flights would no longer operate. Instead of the direct onward flight, the family was assigned a journey with a two-hour-and-40-minute stopover in Bengaluru. The revised return itinerary involved an even longer halt of around 11 hours in the city.The complainant told the commission that the sudden changes caused considerable mental distress to the family and disrupted their holiday plans. He also alleged that the airline made no arrangements for accommodation or other assistance during the extended stopover, leaving him to pay for it himself.The airline's counsel appeared before the commission, but the company did not submit its written version within the prescribed 45-day period. The commission therefore closed its right to file a response. Examining the case, the commission found that the airline had referred to winter schedule changes and operational reasons but had not substantiated why the confirmed flights had to be cancelled and rescheduled. It also pointed out that airlines have a responsibility to provide necessary assistance to passengers when flights are delayed, diverted or cancelled for valid reasons.The commission specifically took note of the family's expenditure during the 11-hour stopover in Bengaluru, observing that the airline had failed to arrange the necessary facilities. Since the passengers had eventually undertaken the journey using the revised flights, the commission considered compensation appropriate rather than treating the entire travel as a failed service. It directed the airline to pay Rs 60,000, working out to Rs 15,000 for each of the four passengers, besides Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses. articles.title: A sister stuck in Riyadh, a family waiting in India: The human cost of Saudi flight ban
articles.summary: Indian airlines have again extended their cancellations to Saudi Arabia as conflict in the region continues.
articles.body: Indian airlines have again extended their cancellations to Saudi Arabia as conflict in the region continues. For families on both sides of the route, the delay has meant missed visits, longer journeys and a constant worry about what comes next.For Indian families with relatives in Saudi Arabia, planning a trip home now begins with a question no booking page can answer: when will the planes fly again?A route that keeps closingAir India and Air India Express have extended the suspension of their flights to and from Jeddah until November 30, citing the security situation in Saudi Arabia. Jeddah services had earlier been cancelled until November 24, while flights to Riyadh and Dammam were already cancelled until November 30."Due to the prevailing situation in the region, Air India and Air India Express flights to and from Jeddah, Dammam and Riyadh will remain suspended until 30 November 2026," Air India said in a post on X on Monday.The other Indian carriers on the route have taken similar steps. On November 18, IndiGo extended the cancellation of flights connecting Saudi Arabian cities until November 30. Akasa Air has cancelled its flights to and from Riyadh and Jeddah until the same date.With four airlines grounding the same routes for the same period, families who depend on direct flights have few easy options left.The conflict behind the cancellationsThe suspensions follow months of escalating violence. In recent months, various Saudi Arabian cities and infrastructure have come under attack from the Houthis, the Iran-aligned group fighting the Saudi-backed government in Yemen. Since the fighting with the kingdom escalated over the summer, the Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi oil facilities, including the Jazan refinery, which was attacked again in the latest incident. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said an attack on an oil refinery in the kingdom's southwest killed a Nepalese worker.The latest incidents mark a further escalation, with strikes from both sides targeting airports, energy facilities and other civilian and economic infrastructure.The violence is not one-sided. Saudi airstrikes hit western and southwestern Yemen overnight, according to Houthi officials and media. Anees al-Asbahi, a spokesperson for the Houthi-run health ministry, said multiple strikes across Taiz province killed four people, including a child, and blamed Saudi Arabia. The Associated Press said it could not independently verify the claims made by al-Asbahi or by Al-Masirah, the rebel-run television channel.Residents of Sanaa, the rebel-held capital, described a life of recurring explosions. "We have to endure these sounds every now and then, and they have health implications for our kids," said Khalil al-Makhlafi, who lives in the southern part of the city, near military camps.The conflict could widen further. The Houthis threatened to attack Saudi ports if the Yemeni port of Hodeidah came under attack. "The port of Hodeidah handles 90 percent of imported goods into Yemen. If it is closed, it could bring the humanitarian situation to the brink of collapse," said Al Jazeera's Yousef Mawry, reporting from Sanaa.A sister in Riyadh and a journey that grew longerFor Saad, the effect of the flight ban is personal. His sister and her husband live in Riyadh. They were supposed to travel to India because of a family emergency, but could not.Their only option was to go to Dubai from Riyadh and take a flight from there. "Usually it's a 5-6 hour journey which would have taken more than 20 hours. So they postponed it," Saad said.The couple is still in Riyadh, and the delay has left the family caught between two worries. "They're still stuck there since they can't make it to India. There's also a worry that if they do come, they won't be able to return because of the tense situation," he said.Saad said his sense of the risk has changed as the conflict has moved closer to the city. "The situation previously remained manageable as strikes were confined to refineries and airports located at a distance from the urban center. However, the landscape has shifted with recent targeting of central city locations, leading to heightened apprehension," he said.He now speaks to his sister more often than he used to. "I make it a point to call her twice daily to ensure that she is doing well," he said.Fear, then a fragile calm in KuwaitThe effects of the conflict are felt beyond Saudi Arabia. A man from India who works in Kuwait told TOI that the regional conflict upended his plans too.He last travelled from Kuwait to India on September 26, 2025, and returned in November 2025. His next trip was planned for March 2026, a short vacation during Holi. "Unfortunately, the conflict started around the same time, and I had to cancel my travel plans," he said.He said Kuwait International Airport was affected by a drone attack around that period, which disrupted operations. Terminal 4 later partially resumed, but flights were limited to certain destinations, and ticket prices were extremely high. "Naturally, there was considerable panic among the public, especially among expatriates who wanted to return to their home countries," he said.Kuwait's distance from Iran, approximately 180 to 200 kilometres, added to the anxiety. People worried about possible escalation, and safety advisories and precautionary guidelines were being circulated.Mobile phone alerts became part of daily life. "Whenever there was an air threat, emergency sirens would sound on our phones. Sometimes, we received these alerts several times during the night, even around 20 times," he said.He credits the authorities with keeping the country running. Air defence systems intercepted incoming threats, and the government maintained food supplies, accommodation arrangements and other essential services. There were some concerns about water supply and possible communication disruptions after damage to undersea fibre-optic cables, but he said these did not significantly affect daily life."Initially, there was certainly fear and uncertainty. However, I believe the Kuwaiti authorities handled the situation responsibly," he said. "At present, I feel much more comfortable compared to the initial period of the conflict. From what I can see, the threat level has reduced significantly, and our daily life and work are almost back to normal."He added that people still follow official safety instructions. "Of course, we remain alert and follow official safety instructions, but I do not feel the same level of panic that we experienced initially," he said.Families watching the news from IndiaFor relatives at home, news bulletins have been harder to watch than the situation itself, as the Kuwait-based worker found. He is in touch with his family almost every day, by phone and video call. During the conflict, they grew very worried after watching the news."They often told me that I should return to India as soon as possible and questioned why I needed to continue staying in Kuwait when the situation was uncertain," he said.He said he understood their concern but could not act on it. "I explained that leaving a job suddenly was not a practical option, especially during that difficult period when travelling was also very challenging," he said.Saad's family faces a similar tension. Calls are frequent, yet they cannot ease the distance. The family wants the couple home, but the fear of being unable to return keeps them from pressing the point.Safety against salaryBehind these decisions lies a choice many Indian families in the Gulf know well. The man in Kuwait said his decision to stay or leave rests mainly on two things: the security situation and his professional responsibilities."If the situation becomes seriously unsafe, I would certainly consider returning to India," he said. "However, at present, things are gradually returning to normal, and I feel comfortable continuing my work here."The second factor is work at home. "Finding a job with a comparable salary and suitable working conditions in India is not easy. I have family responsibilities, so maintaining my employment and financial stability is very important," he said.For now, he intends to stay, and to visit his family when he can. "As long as the situation remains safe and stable, I would prefer to continue working in Kuwait. We also take our vacations from time to time and visit our families in India," he said.His reasoning reflects how many families weigh the risk. "Ultimately, our priority is safety, but we also have to think about our families, careers and financial responsibilities," he said.Waiting on a dateThe latest suspension is due to run until November 30, but the pattern so far gives families little reason to plan around it. Air India's cancellation of Jeddah flights, which first ran until November 24, was extended to November 30 within days, and the other carriers have moved their dates in a similar way.For Saad's sister and her husband in Riyadh, and for thousands of others in the Gulf, the wait continues. A family emergency has been postponed, a festival has been missed, and a short flight home now means a long detour or no journey at all.Until the skies over the region settle, the suitcases stay packed.You use AI every day. articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday issued contempt notices to top officers of the Tamil Nadu government over their failure to follow its order to light the Karthigai Deepam lamp atop the Deepathoon.Calling Tamil Nadu government's move a prima facie contempt of SC's order, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul Pancholi expressed "pain and anguish" and warned that those who try to create constitutional chaos will not be spared."The first thing which comes to our mind is to express the word ALAS! as it would be relevant and appropriate to express in the present scenario. We say so for reasons assigned hereinafter and we say so with pain and anguish," the bench said.Also read: 'Deepam to be lit tomorrow': Furious SC suspends temple trust, asks CRPF to step in"The time has come to deal with the situation with an iron hand as it will lead to constitutional chaos," it added.The apex court said that the executive authorities in the state were "acting on diktats of their political boss" and held that a prima facie contempt case was made out.The bench also suspended the board of trustees of the temple and appointed two retired HC judges, Justice S Vaidyanathan and Justice V Parthipan, as receivers to take over the management of the temple.The SC also handed over the security of Arulmigu Subramaniaswamy temple and Thiruparankundram hill to CRPF.The Supreme Court also directed that the traditional Karthigai Deepam lamp be lit atop the Deepathoon on Saturday.The development came after the ceremonial lamp was lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Ucchi Pillayar temple, rather than at Deepathoon, despite the Supreme Court's order.On November 20, a bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi permitted the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam lamp at Deepathoon on November 24 as a one-time interim arrangement. articles.title: The largest art heist in history happened in 81 minutes. The case is still unsolved
articles.summary: Inside Boston’s storied Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, masterpieces by Titian, Rembrandt and John Singer Sargent greet hundreds of visitors each day, but s...
articles.body:
Inside Boston's storied Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, masterpieces by Titian, Rembrandt and John Singer Sargent greet hundreds of visitors each day, but some walls among the intimate galleries look hauntingly different. Gilded, ornate frames hang empty as a quiet reminder, the museum says, that the search for 13 stolen priceless works — missing in the world's largest unsolved art heist — won't end until every piece is returned.

"This is a sign of hope. We believe that the works will be there again," said Anthony Amore, art theft expert and, for the last 21 years, director of security and chief investigator at the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum. "It's a reminder that this is the only proper home for these stolen works."

The stolen collection is valued today at nearly $1 billion, according to retired FBI investigator Geoffrey Kelly, who spent 22 years leading the FBI's efforts to solve what the agency has called the largest single property crime in US history.

In over 36 years, the works of art have never been recovered and no one was ever charged with the crime, yet the case remains one of the most extraordinary unsolved mysteries, still looms large in public memory and remains a chilling blueprint that continues to inform modern investigations as more violent art crimes have made headlines across Europe.

"The world loves art heists, as you can see with what's happening in the news lately with the Louvre robbery and all these recent museum thefts that have occurred throughout Europe , people love it," said Kelly, who wrote a book about the Gardner Museum investigation called " Thirteen Perfect Fugitives ."

A St. Patrick's Day weekend heist in Boston

On the night of March 17, 1990, Boston was deep in the revelry of St. Patrick's Day celebrations, and police officers were spread thin across the city, according to Kelly.

Just before 1:30 a.m. on March 18, two men in Boston Police Department uniforms arrived at the employee entrance of the museum and rang the night bell, Kelly said. The men told the night watchman they were responding to a disturbance call. Inside Richard "Rick" Abath faced a decision that would become one of the most scrutinized moments in the history of the infamous art heist. Against museum policy, Abath unlocked the door and let them in.

"They were standing there in their hats and coats and badges, and they looked like police, and I buzzed them into the museum," Abath told CNN in an exclusive 2013 interview .

Once inside, the men instructed the guard to call his colleague to join them. When the second guard arrived, the officers told the two guards they were under arrest. They were handcuffed, duct-taped and secured in the museum's basement.

"He finished cuffing me, and he cuffed my partner and very dramatically said, 'Gentlemen, this is a robbery,'" Abath recalled.

Far from being police officers, the men were criminals.

They walked down the hallway to the museum's Dutch Room, where they took six works, including three Rembrandts and a Vermeer.

One thief stayed behind in the Dutch Room and carefully removed some of the paintings from their matting and frames, although two of the Rembrandts were simply cut out.

The other thief headed out of the room back down the hallway to the Early Italian Room and through the Raphael Room. He went back and forth several times, passing by famous works of art, including two Raphaels – "it's a great mystery to the theft," Amore said.

He made it to the Short Gallery, where he took five sketches by Degas and a finial from the top of a flag from Napoleon's 1st Regiment.

An oil painting by Édouard Manet was taken from the Blue Room on the first floor.

Taking their time, the thieves stole 13 irreplaceable works of art in 81 minutes.

In the nearly 34 years following the robbery until his death in 2024 , Abath, who was 23 at the time, was never charged with a crime and consistently maintained he was not involved, though he was questioned by authorities many times.

His longtime lawyer said despite the regulations, Abath opened the door because he thought police officers had told him to.

"If on the one hand I have these museum regulations, and on the other hand there is what appears to be a Boston cop staring at me through the glass portal in the door, telling me to open up, the choice to me is very easy," said George Gormley, who represented Abath at numerous grand jury appearances over the years.

The accusations followed Abath his entire life, according to Gormley.

"You never get your reputation back wholly," Gormley said. "He was a good guy who was trying to live a lawful law-abiding life that was sort of cabined in by all of this."

Whoever was behind the theft, they were never jailed for the crime.

In cinematic blockbusters, art heists are pulled off by refined criminal syndicates like in the Warner Bros. classic " The Maltese Falcon" or by gentlemen art thieves like Thomas Crown , a billionaire who steals priceless paintings for the sheer thrill instead of money, but according to Kelly, the Gardner perpetrators were simply local criminals, known to authorities.

"They were part of the crew of a guy named Carmello Merlino, who was running a drug operation in the Dorchester section of Boston," Kelly said. "They were local mobsters."

In February 1999, the FBI arrested Merlino and three associates in an elaborate undercover sting involving an informant in Merlino's crew, according to court documents. The sting targeted a planned $50 million armored car depot robbery in Easton, Massachusetts.

Prominent Massachusetts defense lawyer Martin Leppo represented Merlino and his crew and told filmmakers of the documentary series "This Is a Robbery: The World's Biggest Art Heist" that federal agents used the sting as leverage to close the Gardner case and recover the stolen artwork.

"They did everything to make an arrest. They set up that sting, and said to them after they were arrested, 'Give up the paintings, you walk out,'" Leppo said.

Merlino died in 2005, according to Federal Bureau of Prisons records , and Leppo died in 2024.

Whoever stole the paintings may have done so for their own leverage, Kelly said.

While the movies might evoke a wealthy oligarch sitting in a secret gallery, swirling cognac surrounded by priceless stolen art, Kelly says the Gardner Museum investigation, and many others he's been involved in as a founding member of the FBI's Art Crime Team, simply don't bear that out.

There's no real market for selling famous stolen paintings, Kelly said. But in Boston at the time, they were used as bargaining chips for thieves who wanted a so-called get out of jail free card.

"I think that was the intention here. They were going to hold on to them for a while, and maybe use it as leverage for any crimes that they were arrested for down the road," Kelly said.

Amore echoed this sentiment, noting stolen masterpieces rarely find legitimate buyers.

"Nobody buys these," he said. "They end up hidden for some sort of future, undefined use. That could be any number of things, including use as a 'get out of jail free' card or as collateral in some illicit trade."

In 2013 , the FBI said it was confident it knew the identities of the thieves, who had local mob ties. The art, it said, was transported to Connecticut and then the thieves tried to sell the works in Philadelphia before the trail went cold.

Why the FBI and local authorities weren't able to make an arrest or recover the pieces, even though they thought they knew who did it , is due to the case drawing too much attention, Kelly said.

"There were three, probably four people involved in the heist who were murdered within a year and a half of the robbery occurring," Kelly alleged. "I think that ends up having a chilling effect on anybody who harbors any aspirations to come forward with information as a result."

In 2015, Peter Kowenhoven, the FBI's assistant special agent in charge in Boston, told The Associated Press the thieves were dead, but declined to identify them.

Kelly was assigned to the Gardner Museum case 12 years after the crime occurred, and seven years after the statute of limitations expired, which is the period in which someone could be charged with a crime for the robbery.

"You don't have anything to hang over somebody's head, and it becomes very difficult," he said, adding the case had gone cold.

Kelly's mission was the recovery of the priceless works of art.

In most art thefts, stolen artwork is typically recovered soon after the crime, according to Kelly. On the other hand, he said, sometimes the pieces come to light many years later.

"If you don't get a recovery during that finite period of time, immediately after a robbery occurs, then it becomes generational," he said. "It's going to be because somebody passes away, somebody gets locked up, families going through grandpa's belongings after he passes on and they find something up in the attic, or they open up a safe deposit box."

Kelly believes the 13 works are still out in the world, and that one day, they will be recovered.

"There's so many examples of artwork that's recovered decades, even centuries after it was stolen," he said.

For example, Kelly pointed to an original Leonardo da Vinci painting called " Salvator Mundi ," which went missing after an auction in 1763, but was recovered by American art dealers Robert Simon and Alexander Parish after 242 years.

Stories like that one give Kelly hope the Gardner Museum pieces will be found.

"It's 13 pieces that were stolen, and I'm the first one to admit that there are some of the pieces from the Gardner heist that I've never heard of anybody saying that they've seen …" Kelly said. "Although we have had very credible sightings of the ( Christ in) the Storm on the Sea of Galilee , which is Rembrandt's seascape."

The Gardner Museum's security and investigations chief shares Kelly's position.

"Often the public and the media assume that because they haven't heard anything that nothing is happening. Reality is quite different," Amore said. "I do not believe it is 'unsolvable.' At this point, it is a search for the location of the art."

A change in tactic and target could thwart stolen art recovery

As high-profile masterpieces are generally unsellable on the open market, according to experts, thieves of the Gardner Museum heist era were likely forced to hide the canvases away intact, treating them as shadow currency or future legal leverage. Amore says the most recent high-profile art thefts are even more concerning, as they break this mold.

"The Gardner theft involved a ruse and the thieves took their time. The others were brutish and quick," Amore said.

In Europe, "the vast majority have been quick smash-and-grab sorts of crimes," he said.

There has been a "disturbing" rise in the theft of culturally significant jewelry, Kelly said, including the 2025 robbery of the world famous Louvre in Paris. Men used an angle grinder and a handheld cutting and grinding power tool to break the window, clambered into one of the most ornate rooms in the museum and smashed two display cases, grabbing nine pieces of Napoleonic-era jewelry, including tiaras, necklaces and earrings adorned with sapphires, emeralds and diamonds worn by the 19th century queens of France. It took robbers four minutes to get in and leave with the loot, prosecutors said.

"Of course the Louvre, they went to steal jewelry because while you can't take a Rembrandt and cut it up into 100 pieces and sell the pieces off, you can take a million dollar piece of jewelry, break it down, recut the gems and melt down the settings … of course more than the monetary value is the cultural significance and importance of these pieces," Kelly said.

This, according to Kelly, is the way criminals can monetize stolen jewelry in a way they can't with well-known paintings or sculptures.

Adding to the temptation for a quick jewelry bust over stolen paintings is, at least in the US, a glaring disadvantage to thieves.

"Our stolen property laws dictate that you never have clear title to stolen property," Kelly said. "The victim is always going to have greater rights to that object than even an innocent third party purchaser, and so that's the reason why the FBI still works this case."

With few exceptions, there is no time limit on the true owner's right to reclaim stolen art. The FBI's ongoing investigation isn't about criminal prosecution — it's about bringing those artworks home to the Gardner Museum, Kelly said.

Hope remains for the return of the Gardner Museum works

As for the priceless works of art lost in the Gardner Museum heist, both experts CNN talked to agreed the masterpieces will someday be recovered.

"High-value, highly recognizable works of art have a higher incidence of recovery than lesser-known works. There is reason to believe all of the above will eventually return to their rightful homes. But it can be a long game," Amore said.

"Investigators and museums must never give up on their masterworks," he added.

As for the European heists, Amore said the French and Italian police are "excellent at investigating art theft" and he believes they will eventually recover much of the stolen pieces.

After marveling at how other works of art have been returned hundreds of years later, like da Vinci's "Salvator Mundi," Kelly put it another way.

"They're out there somewhere. I'm confident they weren't destroyed," he said.

The worth of some of the world's most culturally significant pieces isn't always reflected in their market value, said Kelly, who spent over two decades searching for the Gardner masterpieces, yet they remain vital to humanity.

"It's part of our shared history … It's who we are. It defines us, and it's very important."

articles.title: A longtime cruise passenger sued Royal Caribbean over a $405 car cleaning bill after claiming Celebrity staff directed him to an open parking lot; the cruise line subsequently banned him and his wife for life
articles.summary: A parking arrangement that seemed like a minor inconvenience before a Caribbean holiday turned into an expensive dispute for a Florida couple.
articles.body: A parking arrangement that seemed like a minor inconvenience before a Caribbean holiday turned into an expensive dispute for a Florida couple. After returning from a seven-night cruise aboard Celebrity Apex, the passenger found his Ford Expedition covered in hardened white deposits that he believed were sea salt. He subsequently spent $405 on washing and detailing the vehicle before seeking reimbursement from Celebrity Cruises. When the company refused, he pursued the matter through arbitration before taking it to a small claims court. The dispute eventually had consequences far beyond the original bill. Royal Caribbean, Celebrity's parent company, informed the passenger and his wife that they were no longer welcome aboard its ships.Port Canaveral cruise parking takes an unexpected turn for Celebrity Cruises passengerEric J. and his wife arrived at Port Canaveral in Florida to board Celebrity Apex for a seven-night Caribbean sailing. The couple had used the port's parking facilities for years, generally preferring the covered garage. On this occasion, however, the garage was full.Eric said he was directed towards an uncovered overflow parking area by people he believed were Celebrity Cruises employees. He parked his Ford Expedition there before taking a shuttle to the cruise terminal with his wife. Although he was unhappy about having to leave the vehicle outdoors, the couple proceeded with their holiday.The concern resurfaced when they returned. According to Eric, his vehicle was covered in hard white spots, which he identified as deposits of sea salt, according to Consumer Rescue. He believed prolonged exposure to the coastal conditions had affected the paintwork and wanted the marks removed before they caused further deterioration.According to Consumer Rescue, Eric initially spent $35 at a local car wash. The service did not remove the salt deposits to his satisfaction, prompting him to arrange professional detailing at home for another $370.Celebrity Cruises passenger seeks $405 reimbursement for car cleaningReportedly, Eric subsequently hired a mobile car detailing company to work on the vehicle. The service included professional handwashing and bug removal, along with other detailing work. The invoice came to another $370, bringing his total spending to $405.Once the work was completed, Eric was satisfied with the result. He then turned to Celebrity Cruises, asking the company to reimburse him for the two cleaning services. His argument was that the vehicle had been exposed to the conditions because he had followed directions given at the cruise terminal. The company suggested that he examine his cruise contract, which made clear that parking at the port was not included in the cruise arrangements.The parking facilities at Port Canaveral are operated by the Canaveral Port Authority, rather than Celebrity Cruises or its parent company, Royal Caribbean Group. The cruise line's position was that the responsibility for the parking arrangement did not fall within its contractual obligations.Royal Caribbean passenger files arbitration demand over $405 car cleaning billThe refusal did not end Eric's attempt to recover the money. After examining his cruise agreement, he found a clause referring to arbitration and decided to approach the American Arbitration Association (AAA), an organisation that administers arbitration and mediation proceedings. He submitted a ‘Demand for Arbitration’ against Royal Caribbean, including photographs of the vehicle, his parking receipt, the two cleaning bills and a copy of his cruise contract. He also paid a $225 filing fee to initiate the process.According to Consumer Rescue, the AAA required Royal Caribbean to pay a further $375 fee before the complaint could proceed. By this stage, the dispute had grown beyond the original cleaning expense, with the combined fees and detailing costs taking the amount involved above $1,000.However, the AAA did not proceed with the complaint. About a month after Eric submitted his demand, its Consumer Filing Team informed him that it would not administer the case. Its communication said either party could choose to take the dispute to the appropriate court.Royal Caribbean gives longtime passenger a lifetime ban after lawsuitSoon after filing the paperwork, he received a telephone call from someone identifying himself as a Royal Caribbean representative. Eric initially thought the company might finally be contacting him to discuss compensation or settle the disagreement. Instead, he was informed that he and his wife had been permanently banned from sailing with Royal Caribbean and its affiliated cruise brands.For Eric, the announcement was particularly difficult to accept because of his history with the company. He told Consumer Rescue that he had been sailing with Royal Caribbean for more than 20 years and had never previously encountered a problem. He and his wife were members of the Crown and Anchor Society's Diamond-level loyalty programme and frequently travelled in suites.The ban meant losing the privileges accumulated through those years of cruising. Eric described the situation as a misunderstanding and hoped the company would reconsider its decision.Why the passenger believed the cruise line was responsibleEric later approached consumer advocate Michelle Couch-Friedman, founder of Consumer Rescue, asking for assistance in getting the ban reversed. In his account, he maintained that Celebrity's customer service team had directed him to the contract when he sought compensation. He believed the contract's dispute-resolution provisions meant that arbitration was the appropriate next step. When the AAA declined to administer the case, he understood its response to mean that court proceedings were the remaining option.He also argued that the cruise line had failed to respond to the arbitration notice, leaving him with little choice but to continue with the claim. In correspondence shared with Couch-Friedman, he said the couple had followed the procedures set out in their agreement and had not expected to be banned for doing so.Eric indicated that he was prepared to withdraw the claim if that would help restore his relationship with the cruise line. He wanted his previous customer status and associated benefits back.The port authority's warning that vehicles were parked at owners' riskCouch-Friedman contacted the Canaveral Port Authority to establish who operated the parking facilities and what responsibility it accepted for vehicles left there. The authority confirmed that passengers using its parking areas received a disclaimer printed on the reverse of their payment receipts. It stated that the authority was not responsible for vehicles or personal belongings, including losses or damage resulting from circumstances such as adverse weather.Eric had submitted a copy of his parking receipt as part of his evidence. The front identified the Canaveral Port Authority as the parking operator. According to Couch-Friedman's account, the document therefore raised a fundamental problem with his decision to pursue Royal Caribbean over the incident. The parking was not operated by Celebrity, and the receipt contained a warning that vehicles were left at the owner's risk. The claim also relied on Eric's belief that cruise employees had directed him to the outdoor facility, something that did not establish that the cruise line operated or controlled the parking area.The $370 detailing invoice described a deluxe cleaning service, including bug removal and work intended to improve the vehicle's appearance and protect it against the elements.Consumer advocate questions passenger's legal argumentsCouch-Friedman said she could not establish why Royal Caribbean should be responsible for the cost of cleaning a vehicle parked in a facility operated by the port authority. She also challenged Eric's interpretation of the AAA communication. The association had said it would not administer the case and that either party could take the dispute to court. It had not instructed him to file a lawsuit, nor had Royal Caribbean advised him to pursue legal action over the cleaning bill.During their exchanges, Couch-Friedman raised the possibility that artificial intelligence might have influenced the way Eric was handling the complaint. She said she had encountered other consumer disputes involving legal-sounding arguments and demands that appeared to rely on incorrect information generated by AI tools.Eric did not confirm or deny using AI when she asked him directly. He continued to maintain that he had followed the instructions provided by the cruise line and the arbitration organisation. Couch-Friedman eventually told him that she considered the complaint to be without a sound basis and could not help him secure a reversal of the ban while the lawsuit remained active.Florida court dispute could add legal fees to Royal Caribbean car wash caseDespite the consumer advocate's assessment, Eric did not agree to abandon his position. In a later message, he again said he was willing to withdraw the claim in the hope of repairing the relationship with Royal Caribbean. The case was still on the court docket at the time of Couch-Friedman's report. She said she would be interested to see whether Royal Caribbean sent its lawyers to contest the matter. She also pointed out that Florida courts can, in certain circumstances, order a plaintiff to pay the defendant's legal fees if a lawsuit is found to be frivolous.For the couple, the disagreement had moved a long way from the original $405 expenditure. What began as a complaint about an uncovered parking space had developed into a small claims dispute and a permanent exclusion from Royal Caribbean, Celebrity Cruises and Silversea. Whether the cruise line will reconsider the ban remains uncertain.Disclaimer: This article is based on a report by Michelle Couch-Friedman, founder of Consumer Rescue. The Times of India has not independently verified the passenger's account, the allegations concerning the vehicle or the status and outcome of the legal proceedings.You use AI every day. articles.title: A UK developer planned to build 32 homes on a £2.45 million site but missed a nine-month planning deadline; the High Court has now allowed the seller to keep its £245,000 deposit
articles.summary: A property deal involving plans for 32 homes has ended with a developer losing a £245,000 deposit after the High Court ruled that it had failed to meet a
articles.body: A property deal involving plans for 32 homes has ended with a developer losing a £245,000 deposit after the High Court ruled that it had failed to meet a deadline written into its contract. Thirteen Homes had agreed to buy land from Whitburn Estates for £2.45 million, with the purchase dependent on planning permission and other conditions. But the agreement also required the developer to submit a planning application within nine months. When Thirteen later attempted to end the deal and recover its money, the seller challenged the move. In a judgment handed down in May 2026, the court found that the buyer could not rely on a termination right while it remained in breach of its own obligations.UK developer's £245,000 deposit dispute over 32-home projectThe dispute concerned the former Whitburn Lodge and adjoining land in the North East of England. As reported under England and Wales High Court, an agreement dated 28 January 2022, Whitburn Estates Limited agreed to sell the property to Thirteen Homes Limited for £2.45 million. The proposed development was expected to include 32 homes.The purchase was conditional. The parties had agreed that certain requirements, including planning permission and the release of a restriction affecting the land, would need to be dealt with before the contract became unconditional. The parking restriction was significant because it affected the proposed layout, including 17 of the planned plots.Thirteen paid a £245,000 deposit, which was held by Whitburn's solicitors, DWF Law LLP, as stakeholder. The contract also set out a separate obligation: the developer had to submit its planning application within a target period of six months and no later than nine months after the agreement was signed. That final date was 28 October 2022.Developer failed to resolve parking restriction before planning deadlineThe parking restriction had to be addressed through negotiations with British Coal, which had an interest in the restriction. Thirteen wanted it released before proceeding with the planning application. Its position was that it could not sensibly submit an application for the development while the restriction remained unresolved.The developer did take steps towards preparing its application. It engaged planning consultants and other professionals, commissioned reports and carried out work on the proposed scheme. By October 2022, much of the preparatory work had been completed. The judge later found that, by 22 October, Thirteen had incurred the necessary costs and completed the work required to submit the application, apart from the planning fees payable on filing and a further £4,500 (plus VAT), for its planning consultant to progress the application. But the application was not submitted.The court examined the efforts made to secure the release of the restriction. The evidence showed that Thirteen had contacted British Coal earlier in 2022, but its follow-up efforts were limited. Between 25 August and 28 October, it did not write to or otherwise contact the organisation. The employee who had been handling the matter left Thirteen in early October, and the judge found that the negotiations were not properly taken forward after his departure.Thirteen had also not instructed its own valuation surveyor, made an offer to pay for the release or taken steps to locate an older conveyance relevant to the restriction. The judge considered that a determined purchaser would have continued chasing British Coal and dealt with the associated costs more promptly. He was satisfied that, had Thirteen taken those steps, the restriction could have been released by the October deadline or, at the latest, by January 2023.High Court rejects developer’s argument for more time to applyThe nine-month deadline expired on 28 October 2022. Thirteen still had not submitted the application, and it did not do so later. The developer argued that its obligation to apply for planning permission should be understood in the context of the unresolved parking restriction. It said the contract should be read as allowing more time if it had made reasonable efforts to obtain the release but had not succeeded. It also argued that it should not have been required to apply if British Coal refused to lift the restriction.Whitburn disputed that interpretation. Its position was that the planning application deadline was a separate, unconditional obligation. The contract did not make submission dependent on the release of the parking restriction.Mr Justice Leech agreed with the seller on this point. He found that the agreement imposed an independent obligation to submit the application by 28 October 2022. The parties had negotiated detailed conditions dealing with planning permission and the restriction, but had not made the application deadline conditional on securing the release. The judge also rejected the proposed implied terms put forward by Thirteen.High Court examines whether seller waived missed planning deadlineWhitburn did not immediately terminate the agreement when the October deadline passed. The evidence showed that its representative, John Wade, still wanted Thirteen to submit the planning application and hoped the project could move forward.In correspondence between November 2022 and February 2023, Wade continued asking for updates and encouraging the developer to make progress. The court accepted that his communications gave Thirteen the impression that Whitburn would not immediately treat the missed deadline as a fundamental breach and would allow a reasonable period for late compliance.The developer argued that Whitburn had waived the breach and could not later rely on it to challenge the buyer's attempt to terminate the agreement. The judge accepted that Whitburn had waived the breach to a limited extent. The seller's conduct had indicated that it was prepared to give Thirteen more time to submit the application. But that did not mean the developer had been released from the obligation altogether.Both sides attempted to bring the agreement to an endThirteen served its first termination notice on 23 March 2023, relying on provisions in the contract that allowed it to bring the agreement to an end in certain circumstances. It sought the return of the £245,000 deposit. Whitburn challenged the notice. It argued that Thirteen could not use the contractual termination provision while it remained in breach of the obligation to submit the planning application. The seller also maintained that the missed deadline amounted to a fundamental breach, giving it grounds to terminate the agreement.Whitburn subsequently entered into a conditional agreement to sell the property to another developer, Lovell. It then served its own termination notice on 21 December 2023.The competing notices became central to the High Court case. Thirteen argued that Whitburn's actions, including its dealings with Lovell and its requests for technical reports, showed that it had already accepted the earlier termination or had itself repudiated the contract. The seller denied that it had accepted Thirteen's notice and said it had reserved its legal position.Mr Justice Leech found that Thirteen's first notice was invalid. The developer remained in breach of the planning application obligation when it served the notice and was therefore not entitled to exercise the relevant contractual termination right.He also found that Whitburn's own notice was valid. The failure to submit the application by the agreed date was a fundamental breach, and the contractual deadline was sufficiently clear for time to be treated as being of the essence.The court rejected the argument that the seller had lost its rightsThirteen relied on the emails exchanged between the parties after the deadline to argue that Whitburn had waived its right to terminate. The court's findings were more limited. The seller had indicated that it would allow additional time for the planning application. But Thirteen did not submit one during that extended period either. The judge found that the waiver did not continue indefinitely and did not prevent Whitburn from relying on the breach once the developer failed to perform.The court also considered whether Whitburn's decision to enter into an agreement with Lovell meant it had affirmed the termination notice served by Thirteen. It rejected that argument. The evidence did not establish that the seller had clearly accepted the buyer's notice or acted in a way that prevented it from relying on the contract.The judge was also not persuaded that Thirteen had suffered a disadvantage by allowing Whitburn and Lovell access to the technical reports. The developer had already incurred the costs of preparing them, and its representative accepted that the reports no longer had further value to Thirteen. The contract also provided for the return of relevant documents following termination.High Court rejects developer’s bid to recover £245,000 depositThirteen argued that the deposit should be repaid under section 49(2) of the Law of Property Act 1925. The provision gives the court discretion to order the return of a deposit in certain disputes involving contracts for the sale of land.However, that discretion is generally reserved for exceptional or special circumstances. The developer argued that its work involved the provision of affordable housing and that losing the deposit would affect the resources available for that purpose. It also relied on Whitburn's earlier willingness to allow more time for the planning application.The judge did not consider these points sufficient. The fact that Thirteen was a developer using public funds to provide affordable homes did not, in itself, justify treating it differently from other parties entering into land transactions. Nor did the limited waiver by Whitburn establish that the seller had accepted the buyer's termination notice. The court therefore refused to order repayment of the deposit. It concluded that Whitburn was entitled to retain the £245,000 under the terms of the agreement, following Thirteen's breach and the seller's valid termination.Disclaimer: This article is based on a publicly available High Court judgment. The Times of India has not independently verified the details beyond the court record.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
