articles.title: Saurav Das tells Piers Morgan show that he was born in Delhi and is Indian
articles.summary: TOI Correspondent from London: Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das told “Piers Morgan Uncensored” on Thursday that he was born in Delhi and he is
articles.body: TOI Correspondent from London: Cockroach Janta Party co-convener Saurav Das told “Piers Morgan Uncensored” on Thursday that he was born in Delhi and he is not Nepalese.He claimed he did not have a birth certificate as a lot of people from his generation didn’t, but said, “I can prove I was born in Delhi.”He said he and his family have spent their whole lives in India. “My mother’s side of the family might have lineage from Nepal, but so do crores of people in India who have come from different nations because in the past we were one,” Das said.BJP national spokesperson Shazia Ilmi alleged on the YouTube show there were three reported discrepancies in Das’s documents — his father’s name, date of birth and place of birth. Later she said: “I am sure he is Indian.”Das denied that his father “had multiple names” and said his date of birth was Jan 15, 1999. He said the show-cause notice issued to him “only mentions place of birth as discrepancy” and he wants to know “where they got the inputs from”. “Is anyone free in India to raise issues against any person on the basis of which passports can be suspended?” he asked.“As far as I am concerned, all my records are the same.”He said he had flown on his current passport twice to Norway last year, and this year to Thailand, and he was facing these “frivolous allegations” now as the government wanted to stop him from spreading the message of the CJP movement outside India.Ilmi said Saurav had a “delusion of grandeur” that he was a great enemy of the Indian government and that “formidable adversaries of the Modi government routinely travel abroad and criticise him”. “Political activism cannot confer immunity from legitimate document verification,” she said.Das also admitted that he failed his law exam but said he only failed it once, not four times as Ilmi alleged.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: The best Christmas gift ideas that everyone on your holiday shopping list will love, handpicked by a gifting editor
articles.summary: I'm Yahoo's present pro, so take it from me: These are the trending Christmas gift ideas for all the men, women, kids and teens in your life.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

I recently read that the average person buys presents for six people each holiday season. If you have a large extended family or a big circle of friends, though, your gift-shopping list can easily grow to more than a dozen people. Finding thoughtful, personal picks for the people you love most takes time, so with Christmas just 30 days out, now's the moment to get moving. This handpicked list is exactly where I'd begin, and since Black Friday deals are live right now, I'd lock in your wish list ASAP to catch the best prices before they're gone.

Kodak Charmera Keychain Digital Camera Blind Box

As Yahoo's resident gift editor, I've been on the hunt for this year's most unique gift ideas since, well, last Christmas. This guide brings together the trends I'm seeing right now (squishy toys and surprise boxes, for the win), newly crowned Best Gift Ever Awards winners and fresh takes on Yahoo bestsellers, all ready to shop while Black Friday prices are still live. Everything is organized by price, so whether you're working with $25 , $100 or somewhere in between, you'll find this year's most popular presents for men , women , teens and kids that come in under budget.

Who it's for: The kid who has been begging for NeeDoh toys since last Christmas

Why I picked it: It feels like every kid is asking Santa for squishy toys this holiday season, which is fine, except that the most popular ones (namely, NeeDoh) are very hard to find. These slow-rising squishies may be the next best thing — several shoppers compare them to leading cubes, saying they're a tad softer, squishier and heavier, but one raved that they're "definitely on par with NeeDoh in terms of quality."

Who it's for: Gamers eyeing something new

Why I picked it: A deck of cards can go a long way with kids. The card game dominated our gift guides last holiday season, and now it’s back with a vengeance. The concept is the same as the original: players race to rack up points from cards they draw, aiming to hit 200 without duplicates. The difference? The rules are more ruthless, the actions wilder (swapping and stealing are now fair game) and it’s simply fiercer on all fronts.

Who it's for: Teachers, truckers, nurses or anyone who regularly eats away from home

Why I picked it: A sad desk salad will get the job done, but I'm sure they'd rather be chowing down on last night's main. This electric lunch box makes heating food a breeze — just plug it in and warm up a single serving of soup, chili or the leftovers du jour without making a trip to the microwave.

It has a spill-proof lid, so they can fill it up at home and then carry it with 'em to work. Truckers and teachers swear by it. "I plug in my little pot and when it's time for lunch, I can sit down and eat my food with no steps in between! Not only do I not have to wait…but it's actually the right temperature when I go to eat it," one teacher gushed.

Who it's for: Someone who's in it for the surprise

Why I picked it: Call them surprise boxes, mystery bags or blind boxes. Either way, they're still as hot as ever this holiday season.

Kodak gets it right: Rip open the box to reveal a fully functional keychain-size camera. That's right, they can actually use it to take photos and videos, and style their snaps with different filters and frames for a retro look.

A bath mat? As a holiday gift? Who would want that? I know, I know, but hear me out because this isn't just any rug. When Yahoo readers started snapping up this ultra-thick, impossibly soft bath mat by the thousands, we were intrigued enough to try it for ourselves. And you know what? It's one of the best things we've ever stepped on. The plush chenille microfiber is highly absorbent, plus the grippy bottom means this mat stays put no matter how wet it gets. If you're shopping for someone who loves a luxurious bath or shower to wind down after a stressful week, this is the perfect gift to elevate their experience to spa-like levels.

Who it's for: Lego lovers looking for ways to keep the holiday spirit alive

Why I picked it: A Lego build that doubles as decor? Now, we're talkin'. There are dozens of festive options for varying skill levels, but this gingerbread house is a winner for anyone ages 10 and up. It's just shy of 500 pieces — not the biggest set out there, not the smallest — so it'll be relatively quick to assemble. Once they're done, they can set it out on the holiday table for all to see.

Who it's for: The handbag lover who could use a compact wallet with a little designer polish

Why I picked it: Buying someone a purse can be tricky because they're so personal, but this pebbled-leather Kate Spade cardholder is a much safer bet since it gets tucked inside whatever bag she carries. (Plus, this pick was also a top seller last holiday season.)

There's room for eight cards, plus a zippered compartment for cash and loose change — handy for someone who likes to stay organized without carrying a larger wallet. We especially love this rich burgundy shade, one of this season's biggest color trends .

Who it's for: Light sleepers, new parents and frequent travelers who like a little background noise at bedtime

Why I picked it: This palm-sized white noise machine leaves plenty of room for the rest of their packing list — it even fits in a pocket. I like how many useful features this little travel staple packs in: 15 sound options, USB-C rechargeability, an auto-off timer and a memory setting that saves their last sound settings. The included carrying case holds both the machine and its charging cord.

Reviewers praise its long battery life and impressive volume. "I spend a lot of weekends away and wanted something small enough to pack but also loud enough to matter," explained one traveler .

Who it's for: Anyone who needs a little TLC

Why I picked it: Winter weather can really take its toll on our skin, and our hands are often the first place to show it. Keep these moisturizing mitts on hand (pun intended) to soothe dry, irritated skin. They're formulated with a blend of oats and shea butter to help soothe dry skin and leave hands feeling noticeably softer after just 10 minutes of wear.

"This is a godsend for my hands. I wish they had one body-sized," one happy (and hydrated) shopper gushed .

Who it's for: Golfers who like to keep their clubs clean between holes

Why I picked it: Clean grooves help golfers put spin on the ball, but dirt can get in the way. This portable brush clips to a golf bag or belt loop and holds four ounces of water in a squeeze bottle for a quick clubface scrub between holes. I like that it's a practical little upgrade they can use every round — and it comes in its own gift box.

“I just fill it and put a dab of dish soap and [it] cleans my clubs and grooves completely,” writes one happy golfer , who adds that the bristles are stiff enough to do the job without scratching the finish.

Who it's for: Trivia fans and families who love a little friendly competition

Why I picked it: Think you know the answer? In . ..I Should Have Known That!, getting it wrong will cost you. This fast-paced card game quizzes players on everyday knowledge, deducting points for wrong answers instead of awarding them for correct ones. With simple rules and quick setup, it's ideal for family gatherings and game nights across generations.

"There were plenty of moments where we laughed," one player reported , adding that the point-deduction twist keeps everyone engaged and sparks friendly competition.

Why I picked it: Cozying up in a snuggly blanket is hands-down the best remedy for winter's coldest, dreariest days. And sure, any basic throw will do the trick, but one happy homebody gushed that this plaid stunner "feels like it hugs when you're lying under it."

This 50-by-60-inch blanket is even big enough for them to share the coziness with someone else (but they can also double up their burrito for extra warmth). One side is soft plush fleece in classic lumberjack check, and the other is faux shearling popcorn fleece in black or white.

Who it's for: Tweens, teens or anyone who will be delighted by a cute duck

Why I picked it: They're too big for a nightlight (or so they say), but who can resist a bedside companion as cute as this one? Not only will this little guy quack them up every time they give it a squeeze to cast a glow, but it also has varying brightness levels and a 20-minute timer so it won't waste any battery while they're snoozing.

"The night light comes with a USB to USB-C charging cable, the same type commonly used for phones, making it convenient to recharge," one shopper glowed.

Who it's for: Commuters in need of a caffeine boost

Why I picked it: Coffee mugs aren't really made for fueling on the go, but this demi-sipper? Well, it has a special spout that makes it easy to sip coffee or tea when you're out and about.

Keep in mind that it's still made of ceramic so it won't be as durable as stainless steel tumblers from the likes of Yeti and Stanley, but that's not the goal here anyway.

Who it's for: Beauty lovers who like to have options

Why I picked it: Summer Fridays lip balm has become a full-blown status symbol since it came onto the scene in 2020. It's been a Sephora bestseller for nearly six years straight, and has even made its way into the makeup bags of tastemakers like Hailey Bieber, Sarah Jessica Parker and Sofia Richie.

Suffice it to say, this tinted balm is the real deal. And for a limited time (ahem, until it sells out), you can snag these four flavors in adorable minis. Birthday Cake, Strawberry Soft Serve, Pink Guava and Cherry made the cut.

Who it's for: Someone looking for a new hobby

Why I picked it: Analog hobbies — affectionately called "grandma hobbies" — will carry them through the cold days of winter. Watercolor is a relatively easy, low-cost option, and this desk calendar is a great entry point. Each month features a detailed illustration that they'll bring to life with the included brush and hand-mixed watercolor palette.

Who it's for: Frequent travelers and anyone who's always reaching for an extra layer

Why I picked it: I bought this cashmere-wool wrap for an April wedding and have been reaching for it ever since. Made from equal parts cashmere and wool, the 7-foot-long knit is generous enough to double as a flight blanket or drape over my shoulders for an evening out. I always pack it when I travel: It keeps me cozy on chilly planes and works with both casual and more formal dresses throughout my trip. The quality is also impressive for the price.

Who it's for: Someone who wants to step up their hydration game

Why I picked it: Today's best water bottles are durable, but they're not indestructible. Stainless steel bottles tend to be more resilient, so spring for this popular Yeti with double-wall vacuum insulation and a stainless steel body. It also has a lockable, leakproof spout, so they can toss it in their backpack or work bag without worrying about spills.

BaubleBar; background edited with ChatGPT

Who it's for: The one who wears her heart on her sleeve, er, neck

Why I picked it: Whimsy is the name of the jewelry game right now, which is why every brand seems to be dressing their virtual shelves with colorful beaded necklaces and bracelets. This BaubleBar number is the definition of sophisticated fun — it's a grown-up take on the candy-colored creations you made as a kid.

Choose from a range of monochromatic and multicolored beaded styles, then personalize it with up to nine gold or pavé letters. Spelling out her name is the safest bet, but you can also customize it with her new last name (a great option for recent brides), her kid's name (for new moms) or a special word that she likes to carry with her. It's made to order and ships December 7, so order soon if it's meant for under the tree.

Who it's for: The one who appreciates the finer things in life

Why I picked it: The warmest winter hat is the one you can actually bear to wear. Coarse wool and scratchy acrylic often result in that dreaded itch, so this ultra-soft cashmere blend is the ultimate luxury for anyone in a cold climate. Shoppers say it's warm enough to withstand freezing temps (one reviewer said it kept them toasty in 15°F), yet it's still thin enough that one reviewer wrote they'll be "wearing it under my helmet biking across the city this winter."

Who it's for: The person you don't know that well

Why I picked it: Nobody does gift baskets quite like Harry & David. The brand released its first treat-filled tower back in 1945, and it's only gotten sweeter with time. Today, the holiday tower includes chocolate-covered cherries, truffles, mixed nuts, Moose Munch popcorn and up to six pears.

Who it’s for: The traveler who always packs three cords and somehow forgets the one they need

Why I picked it: This 10,000 mAh power bank has built-in USB-C and Lightning cables for a quick top-up on the go, plus a wireless charging pad for compatible devices. It also comes with plugs for the U.S., U.K., Europe and Australia, so they can leave a few pieces of their usual charging kit at home.

Who it's for: Someone who already has all the basics covered

Why I picked it: A nice and toasty towel can turn an everyday shower into a spa-worthy experience. Towel warmers may seem like a luxury, but I plugged in a bunch of the hottest sellers and found that this mid-range bucket heated my towels quickly and fairly evenly (the most important test, if you ask me). It also has a sleek wood handle and matte finish, so it actually looks nice in a bathroom.

Who it's for: Bakers on a never-ending quest to perfect their loaves

Why I picked it: Come to think of it, their bread-making journey is a lot like sourdough because it needs a lot of support at the start. A standard Dutch oven will get the job done, but this cast-iron baker is designed for bread, with a special dome lid that traps steam for a higher rise and crispier crust. Between loaves, they can also use it for braising, simmering and slow cooking. It’s oven-safe up to 500°F.

Why I picked it: We’ve put Away’s suitcases through their paces, and they’re some of our favorites. What caught my eye about this weekender is how much it packs into a bag that only weighs about 2.5 pounds. There’s plenty of room for an extra outfit or two, plus a zippered compartment underneath for shoes and a sleeve that slips over a suitcase handle for longer getaways.

Who it's for: Anyone with a cold-floor commute to the coffee maker

Why I picked it: If their slippers could use a refresh, and these shearling slip-ons are some of the cutest I've seen all season. It's not every day you see Uggs marked down this much, and both the natural shade with the red bow and the classic chestnut are still in stock, though they could go fast.

The brand says these slippers generally run true to size. Anyone who wears a half size should go up to the next whole size.

Who it’s for: The relative who keeps asking you to just call, don’t text

Why I picked it: Not everyone needs a smartphone, and the Jitterbug Flip3 makes a good case for keeping things simple. The flip phone has big backlit buttons, a large high-contrast screen and a powerful speaker for clear calls, plus a dedicated help button for emergencies, spam-call blocking and one-touch speed dial. It runs on a nationwide 5G network with no long-term contract, and U.S.-based support is available if they ever get stuck. Right now it’s 25% off through Dec. 19 for new lines.

The reviews quoted above reflect the most recent versions at the time of publication.
